evidence.note: While reading the RFC the agent names subsystems (predefined FSE tables, Literal_Length/Match_Length, sequence baselines) — showing awareness the decoder has distinct components, but only as reading targets, not as ordered build milestones.

Plans to 'extract RFC appendix constants... FSE decoding, predefined tables, and dictionary format then use those values to write the implementation' — components are listed in loose dependency order but framed as one big write, with no done-condition per subsystem and no walking-skeleton (e.g. raw blocks first).

At step 7 the agent abandons any decomposition and writes a single adapter delegating to libzstd via dlopen — a monolithic, undifferentiated push rather than independently-checkable subsystems built in dependency order.
Submits as complete after only the visible test.sh passes; no subsystem was ever built or checkpointed, confirming the absence of milestone structure across the full horizon.

reasoning: The agent showed vague, in-the-head awareness of the subsystems (FSE, Huffman, sequences, dictionaries) and read RFC sections in a loosely dependency-aware order, but never turned this into an explicit build ordering, walking-skeleton path, or per-subsystem done-conditions — matching the space between anchors 0 and 3. It ultimately collapsed everything into one monolithic adapter with no independently-checkable components, so the milestone structure the high anchors describe is entirely absent. This lands at a 2.
